Negative-control diagnostics in the creator log are followed by their expected rejection assertions; they are not suite failures. These results support structural/retained-consumer claims, not expert equivalence or creator gain.

Source identity, observed conduct/recommendation/inference separation, cue-to-method decisions, independent wrong-outcome checks and preserved permissions are explicit. The rationale is calibrated: [Rieseberg's article](https://felixrieseberg.com/how-to-be-more-ambitious-a-tutorial-for-humans-with-models/) supports field methods, raw evidence and outside checks; [FRA's CTA page](https://railroads.dot.gov/human-factors/elearning-attention/cognitive-task-analysis) describes incident accounts and elicitation of expert judgments/cues. Neither is presented as measured benefit of this creator procedure.
